## Can fixed BERT features compete with fine-tuning? {#ft-evidence .ft-slide}

<p class="ft-lead"><strong>CoNLL-2003 named-entity recognition</strong> · BERT-base · development F1 ↑</p>
<table class="ft-research"><thead><tr><th>Adaptation strategy</th><th>Task model / features</th><th>Dev F1</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th>Frozen BERT</th><td>Last hidden layer → BiLSTM + classifier</td><td>94.9</td></tr><tr><th>Frozen BERT</th><td>Concatenated last four layers → BiLSTM + classifier</td><td>96.1</td></tr><tr><th>Full fine-tuning</th><td>BERT-base + token classifier</td><td>96.4</td></tr></tbody></table>
<div class="ft-evidence-points"><p><strong>Finding:</strong> useful pretrained features can support a strong task model without updating BERT.</p><p><strong>Comparison:</strong> the task architectures differ. Frozen features here use a two-layer, 768-dimensional BiLSTM.</p><p><strong>Scope:</strong> these are NER development scores, not sentiment results or proof that full fine-tuning always wins.</p></div>
<p class="s1-source">Selected rows transcribed from <a href="https://aclanthology.org/N19-1423.pdf#page=9">Devlin et al. (2019), §5.3, Table 7</a>. Mean over five random restarts; hyperparameters selected on development data. The selected rows report no uncertainty intervals. Cased WordPiece and maximal available document context.</p>

::: {.notes}
TIME: 5 minutes. Start with the setting, not with the largest number. NER attaches
entity labels to words; later we will build that output interface. F1 evaluates entity
recognition, not binary sentiment accuracy. All three values come from the Dev F1
column. Do not compare 96.1 dev F1 with 92.4 test F1 from another column.
The frozen approach extracts states without changing BERT, then learns a two-layer
768-dimensional BiLSTM and classifier. It is not our head-only linear probe. The
fine-tuned model uses a token-level classifier on the first subtoken and no CRF.
Both conditions use task labels, cased WordPiece, and available document context.
The best displayed frozen configuration concatenates four layers; comparing 94.9
with 96.1 shows that the feature choice matters too. All reported scores are means
of five restarts. No uncertainty intervals are supplied in this table, so do not
assert statistical significance from the small gap. Development data also selected
hyperparameters; this is not an independent final test comparison of all strategies.
Ask: what does this establish? Both reuse strategies are viable in this setting.
What does it not isolate? Updating the encoder alone, because task heads differ.
Practical implication: freezing can permit precomputed representations, but caching
assumes a fixed input, encoder, and deterministic feature-extraction settings.
:::
